::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** July 29th [1867]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54920: 188-189
:::

Dear [Mr Macmillan](people/person_939.qmd),
I am getting well again, and gone to work again.[^1] Clement of Alexandria is the first authority for the robber story, but Eusebius takes it from him. I have a queer old [translation of Eusebius](other_books/otherbook_504.qmd), Socrates and Co - from which I really did expand the account, and so I think I had better leave Eusebius, as it looks less as if it all came out of [Smith’s dictionary](other_books/otherbook_389.qmd) as in fact much necessarily does.

I am glad you and [Mr Masson](people/person_980.qmd) consent to the [Chaplet of Pearls](cmy_books/cmybook_69.qmd) - it really was a material chaplet, and if it were coming at once in a book by itself, I should begin by quoting [Froissart](other_books/otherbook_219.qmd)’s old French about it. I suppose by your account there is power in the [Scotch girl](organizations/other_193.qmd) that wants toning down. 

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: She was working on *The Pupils of St. John the Divine*.
